Hi Marcus — thanks for the clear questions. Below are concrete answers based on our current hosted product and options for Dedicated/Private deployments. I've also attached a short retention table and security brief to this thread.

1) Are prompts and model outputs stored by default on Redwood hosted API? If so, where and for how long?
- Hosted (default): We persist request/response logs (prompts and model outputs) for 30 days by default to support debugging, abuse monitoring, and platform safety. Logs are stored encrypted at rest in our regional object store (AWS S3 in the customer-region by default; for US customers we use us-west-2). Access to these logs is restricted to a small set of operations and security engineers; all access is logged and audited.
- Dedicated: Retention is configurable by contract and we can set shorter retention windows or rolling deletion policies on request.
- Private (on-prem/VPC): Customer-controlled; Redwood control plane can be configured to not persist prompts/outputs if required.

2) Embeddings and derived artifacts
- We do NOT persist embeddings derived from model outputs by default unless the API call explicitly requests storage (e.g., the user calls our embeddings index/store APIs). If you never call the persistent embeddings/index APIs, no embeddings are retained beyond the short-lived inference cache (seconds to minutes).
- If you do use our embeddings/indexing features, retention is configurable; by default, those stored artifacts follow the account retention policy and can be purged on demand.

3) Opt-out of storage for specific routes or whole account
- For Hosted customers, we offer an "no-retain" account flag for enterprise customers under an agreed contract. This enforces that request/response bodies are not written to persistent logs; traces for operational debugging are still available in anonymized form.
- For Dedicated and Private deployments, you can fully disable persistent logging of prompts/outputs or implement custom retention.

4) Encryption and key management
- Transit: All API traffic is TLS 1.2+ encrypted.
- At rest: Data is encrypted using AES-256. For Hosted, we use KMS-managed keys; enterprise customers can opt into customer-managed KMS keys (CMK) for hosted accounts under an enterprise agreement. Dedicated/Private support CMKs and HSM integrations.

5) Data residency
- Hosted: You can choose the region where your data is stored (US or EU regions available today). EU-region hosting keeps persistent logs in EU data centers.
- Dedicated/Private: Data residency is under the customer's control.

6) Audit/logging and access controls
- Access to stored prompts/outputs is RBAC-protected and requires elevated permissions. All access is audited and retained per our audit logging policy.

7) Retention and deletion process
- Deletion: We support on-demand deletion requests at the account level and have an automated purge pipeline for expired logs.
- Retention windows: default hosted = 30 days; can be shortened by contract for Dedicated customers.

Attachments included: redwood-security-brief.pdf (high-level controls), redwood-pii-retention-table.csv (artifact-by-artifact retention and configurable knobs).

If you want, we can map these answers to the specific questions in your questionnaire. Otherwise, we can schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week to go through any regulatory edges.
